title: Whole Flared-Corona Star-Perianth Daffodil
description: One newly authored complete stylised daffodil-like above-ground flowering plant. Three narrow arching basal strap leaves and one continuous bent-neck flower stalk support one forward-facing flower. A real thick-walled flared central corona has a deep open front, closed recessed base and mildly scalloped rim, surrounded by six complete broad tapered star-like perianth segments. The central flower is a genuine hollow trumpet shape rather than an opaque disk, orchid lower lip or rolled leaf bract around a spadix. New whole stalk, leaf and flower surfaces; no old flower box component extracted or petal count used as sole distinction. One static whole plant, zero scenes. No exact species, reproductive microanatomy, pollination, growth, roots, cultivation, toxicity, medicinal or ecological function claim.
